subject: POC: BlueCove connector compatibility & validation workshop
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emma Larson <emma@bluecove.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: POC: BlueCove connector compatibility & validation workshop

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the intro last week. BlueCove's connector looks like a promising fit for a managed connector we want to surface for customers using private deployments. Before we commit to an engineering POC we want to run a short technical validation workshop and align on a modest discovery POC scope.

High-level goals for the session:
- Validate connector auth patterns (KMS/HSM integration and token lifecycle)
- Confirm data flow for KV/prefix caching and whether BlueCove can stream partial responses for low-latency paths
- Run a compatibility smoke of quantized model paths (8-bit/4-bit) and any operator fallbacks
- Agree on the POC success criteria and test fixtures (sample prompts, seq lengths, throughput targets)

Proposed attendees from our side: me (partner eng), Marissa (solutions architect), Evelyn (ops lead). Can you include the BlueCove SE who owns the connector and an implementation lead?

Suggested times: Thu Nov 5 or Fri Nov 6 morning PST. Also if you have a short connector spec or sequence diagram you can drop ahead of the session that would help us prep.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — great to set this up. Confirming our SE (Kenji Suzuki) and our integration PM (Priya Rao) will join.

We can do Thu Nov 5 at 10:00am PST. We'll prepare a short spec and an integration sequence diagram and attach it here for your review.

Quick notes up front: BlueCove supports token-based auth with KMS-wrapped keys (we have a HSM integration via CloudKMS/HSM). Connector supports both streaming and buffered responses; there are a couple of caveats around partial KV eviction when you use aggressive prefix caching — happy to walk through. For quantized paths we do best-effort fallback for operators not available in runtime; we surface a compatibility table in the spec.

Attaching: bluecove-connector-spec.pdf (summary spec), integration-sequence.drawio (diagram)

—Emma Larson

Jonas / Emma — quick pass from an SA perspective.

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 10:20 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached a short POC checklist we'll use to scope the discovery run (tests, success metrics, test data cadence). For the workshop agenda let's aim for:
> 1) 20m architecture walkthrough (BlueCove SE)
> 2) 30m validation scenarios and test harness (joint)
> 3) 20m infra & auth mapping (KMS/HSM, network, VPC peering)
> 4) 10m mutual action plan and next steps

Two quick additions:
- Add an observability acceptance criteria: request-level traces must include model_id, quantization_profile, and route_id so we can map latency regressions to connector behaviour.
- For the KV/prefix caching test, include a synthetic workload that mixes short-response (<128 tokens) and long-tail (2k tokens) to exercise cache hit/miss paths.

Also, can BlueCove confirm whether their connector will respect upstream TTL on cached keys or if it enforces its own expiry semantics? That affects our validation harness.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Emma Larson <emma@bluecove.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: BlueCove connector compatibility & validation workshop

Hi Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks for the notes. To your questions:
- TTL semantics: connector by default respects upstream TTL if set; otherwise it will apply a configurable expiry (default 5m). We'll include a config toggle so you can test both behaviours.
- Observability: we emit request-level metadata via X-Trace headers and can add model_id/quant_profile/route_id to the payload for the POC. We'll demo a small Grafana dashboard during the workshop.
- Quantized operator fallbacks: included in the spec (see table page 3). For operators that fall back to CPU we provide a cost/latency delta estimate.

Attaching our spec again for convenience. We can also throw together a minimal staging plan doc by EOD today if that helps.

Best —
Emma
